paragraphs: Thousands of students and teachers are protesting across France because public high schools are in terrible condition.
Classrooms are overcrowded, buildings are falling apart with leaks and rats, and there are not enough substitute teachers when staff are sick.

The protests began near Paris and spread to many cities. Unfortunately, some protests became very violent. Protesters set fire to bins and damaged school buildings, while riot police used tear gas and grenades to clear the streets. Police arrested thousands of people.

The French Prime Minister said that violence will not fix the school system. With an important presidential election coming in six months, these angry protests show that the country is divided over public education and government spending.

paragraphs: Thousands of students and teachers in France are protesting today. They are angry because high school buildings are old, dirty, and broken. Many classes are full, and there are not enough teachers.

The protests start near Paris and are now everywhere in the country. Sadly, some protests become violent. People burn bins and break school doors. Police must stop them. Thousands of people go to prison, and some people get hurt.
Leaders say that these protests will not help schools. France is voting for a new president in six months. It is a big problem for many people. They are worried about their schools.

words.d: when someone uses force to hurt people or break things
when people choose a new leader or someone for an important job
